identification: Twin-pack box of two 1970s half-litre (50 cl) 75° proof Scotches: Dalmore 12 Years Old Pure Malt (Whyte & Mackay Distillers Ltd label, clear tall bottle, gold screw cap) and Whyte & Mackay's De Luxe blend (double lion label, gold screw cap). The gold box shows both labels, 'Whyte & Mackay's ... Established 1844' and a black 'Half Litre' band. Box text near the base reads '...AY D...' and is partly hidden.
era: 1970s for both bottles. The sources split between early 1970s (Just Whisky) and late 1970s (Whisky Hammer, Whiskybase). None of them dates the half-litre size specifically.
era_evidence: Dalmore: the label features (12 crest, 'Pure Malt', 'Whyte & Mackay Distillers Ltd', 75° proof) match the 26⅔ fl oz 75° proof bottle that Just Whisky describes as 'Old style Dalmore 12 Year Old from the early 1970s' (https://www.just-whisky.co.uk/product/dalmore-12-years-old-whyte-mackay-pure-malt-75-proof-1454470). Whisky Hammer describes the 75 proof 1 litre as 'estimated to have been bottled towards the end of the 1970s' (https://www.whiskyhammer.com/item/6456/Dalmore/Dalmore---12-Year-Old-Pure-Malt-1970s.html). Whiskybase WB90961, 'Golden Label, 75 Proof', 1000 ml, gives Bottled: Late 1970s (https://www.whiskybase.com/whiskies/whisky/90961). Other Whiskybase IDs seen in search results: WB65216 (Golden Label, 26⅔ fl oz / 75.7 cl, 70° proof, no bottling date shown); WB184923 ('Pure Malt Scotch Whisky, Gold label, clear glass, Whyte & Mackay', 750 ml 43%, bottled column 1970); WB208408 ('43 G.L., Gold label, Whyte & Mackay', 750 ml 43%, bottled column 1980). No Whiskybase entry was found for a 50 cl / half-litre Dalmore 12 or a half-litre Whyte & Mackay De Luxe, so I have no Whiskybase ID for either half litre. The SWA 2015 half-litre lot (https://www.scotchwhiskyauctions.com/auctions/85-auction/60848-dalmore-12-year-old-old-style-75-proof-05l/) has a photo of the same clear tall bottle with a gold cap and the same label, and SWA calls it 'An old style Dalmore from the age of the pure malt'. The 1970s 26⅔ fl oz 75° proof bottle at Just Whisky is a squat green bottle with a cork stopper, so the half litre is a different bottle format with the same label. Whyte & Mackay De Luxe: whisky.auction dates a 'Supreme De Luxe' 75.7 cl 40% bottle to the 1970s (https://whisky.auction/auctions/lot/29146/whyte-mackay-de-luxe). I found no source that dates the half-litre De Luxe itself.

viewing_check: 1) Read the box text hidden behind the bottles (the '...AY D...' line at the base) and check every side for 'duty free', 'export' or a market name. 2) Check the Whyte & Mackay label's right-hand side for its strength and size (the photo shows 'Half Litre' on the left, and the right side is cut off). 3) Look at the gold screw caps for rust, dents or seepage stains, and check the inside of the box for old leakage. 4) Fill is at the base of the neck in the photo, which is good for the age, but compare the two bottles side by side. 5) Check the box flaps and corners, since an intact twin pack is the point of difference. 6) Evidence on value is thin: the only same-bottle sale is £80 hammer in April 2015. The best recent sale of the same label is the bigger 26⅔ fl oz 75° proof bottle at £230 hammer (Just Whisky, April 2023). The De Luxe adds little (about £20 to £25 for a 75 cl 1970s bottle).

identification: Pooley 'Butcher's Hill' Single Vineyard Pinot Noir magnum (1.5 L), dark red capsule, label 'Richmond · Coal River Valley, Estate grown & bottled', in a branded Pooley pine box (Est. 1985, Coal River Valley, Tasmania) with straw and brass catches. The vintage is unreadable in the 450x600 photo (the Armitage online image is the same size).
vintage_evidence: Not settled. Enlarging the label shows '20', a narrow third digit and a fourth digit that could be 2 or 7. Both vintages exist: Halliday has tasting notes for Pooley Butcher's Hill Pinot Noir 2012 (https://www.winecompanion.com.au/wineries/tasmania/tasmania/pooley-wines/wines/red/pinot-noir/butchers-hill-pinot-noir/2012) and 2017 (https://www.winecompanion.com.au/wineries/tasmania/tasmania/pooley-wines/wines/red/pinot-noir/butchers-hill-pinot-noir/2017). Halliday titles both 'Butcher's Hill Single Vineyard Pinot Noir', so the 'Single Vineyard' wording doesn't separate them. The label layout matches lot 844's 2017 Cooinda Vale label. The two came from one seller in matching numbered boxes, but I found no page showing Pooley released both as numbered magnums in the same year. CellarTracker label photos for Butcher's Hill 2012 and 2017 sit behind CellarTracker's sign-in wall, so I couldn't compare them. Best fix: read the label in person or ask Armitage.
production: Not found for 2012 or 2017 magnums. For reference, Pooley's own spec sheet for the 2018 Butcher's Hill Pinot Noir Magnum states 'Production: 144 Magnums' (https://secure.withwine.com/Public/File?fileName=upload%2F1597%2Fproduct%2Ffpzf78JkHUKzEi83-aRMtg.pdf&download=False). That's a different vintage and a different number from x/72.
release_price: 750 ml: 2017 Butcher's Hill Pinot Noir A$65 on Pooley's own shop page, Wayback copy of 2 Jan 2019 (https://web.archive.org/web/20190102143209/http://www.pooleywines.com.au/purchase/page/2/). Halliday lists 'price when tasted' as A$65 (2017, tasted 17 Oct 2018) and A$45 (2012, tasted 31 Jan 2014). Magnum: no magnum appears in the archived Pooley shop pages from Jan 2019 or Dec 2019. Null.
drinking_window: Not available. Halliday's drink-from and drink-by dates are members-only for both 2012 and 2017.
drinking_now: No 2024 to 2026 notes captured for Butcher's Hill 2012 or 2017. CellarTracker blocked both wine pages (2017: https://www.cellartracker.com/m/wines/3009550; 2012: https://www.cellartracker.com/m/wines/1901078) behind sign-in. On Delectable's Butcher's Hill page, notes of 9.3 (Ross Bathgate, 23 Dec 2024, 'Mature and Delicious') and 9.3 (Jason Keefer, 11 May 2025, 'still fresh and juicy') don't name a vintage (https://delectable.com/wine/pooley/butchers-hill-pinot-noir).

Pooley states it won the 2012 Tasmanian Vineyard of the Year and was 2012 Pinot Noir Producer of the Year, with 18 golds and 2 trophies at the 2012 Tasmanian Wine Show. That's an award year, not a vintage rating for 2012 Butcher's Hill. Source: Pooley homepage, Wayback copy Jan 2020 (https://web.archive.org/web/20200112073204/https://www.pooleywines.com.au/).

Langtons notes that the Butcher's Hill vineyard at Richmond was established in 2003 and is 6 ha (https://www.langtons.com.au/p/pooley-cooinda-vale-pinot-noir--tasmania-2017-bottle/auc-mas-67682-2017-1.html). Pooley's 2018 magnum spec sheet lists clones 114, 115, 777 and MV6.

viewing_check: 1) Read the vintage on the label in person, or ask Armitage. It decides which ratings apply. 2) Check where the 49/72 is written (box, label or neck tag) and whether there's a certificate or card in the box. 3) Check fill level and the capsule for seepage stains or stickiness, and find out whether the magnum is cork or screw cap. 4) Ask about storage history (cellar or cupboard), since a 2012 would be 14 years old.
